title: Introduce streamlined observability gateway and token-slew meter
author: Maya Sato
description: Motivation: Production SREs and product teams need a lower-latency path for critical telemetry (metrics/traces/log summaries) while also getting fine-grained token-level burst detection per tenant without overwhelming our long-term pipeline. This PR introduces a lightweight Observability Gateway (inference-obsgw) that acts as a first-class intake and router for high-cardinality, production-sensitive signals and a new token-slew meter that detects rapid token-rate surges at the invocation and tenant level. The gateway enables two modes: 1) fast-path shallow enrich+forward for critical signals used in SLO enforcement and alerting and 2) async deep-hydration to the existing telemetry pipeline for storage and long-term analytics. The token-slew meter is implemented as a streaming aggregator that emits burst-anchors and a compact burst fingerprint to downstream rollups for correlation with cost and latency dashboards. Key changes: additions of a small Rust-based gateway service with Prometheus/OTLP endpoints, a lightweight protobuf for compact invocation snapshots, an extension to the trace enrichment pipeline to accept burst anchors, a new Grafana dashboard and alert rules for token-slew events, and CLI tooling to run gateway in private deployments. Backwards compatibility: gateway accepts current OTLP and our existing proto and will fall back to legacy ingestion when feature flag is disabled. Rollout plan: staged Canary on dedicated infra for 48h using ENG-1426 test harness, then progressive enablement by region with throttled sampling windows. Rollback plan: flip feature flag to legacy ingestion and drain gateway for 30m before shutdown. Testing: unit tests for protobuf compatibility, integration tests with the replaybench to verify cost correlation, e2e canary asserts for alerting behavior, and manual QA of dashboard panels. Observability improvements: token-slew meter provides per-tenant burst counts, burst duration histograms, and correlation keys for traces; gateway reduces tail ingestion latency by ~40% in internal benchmarks. Files and areas touched: runtime/telemetry/ (gateway adapter), telemetry/proto/ (compact snapshot schema), observability/ingest/ (forwarder and enrichment hooks), console/grafana/ (new dashboard panels), docs/private-installer/ (gateway deployment example), sdk-telemetry/ (TS/Go client small helper), ci/ (pipeline updates). See commits for details. Impact: improves incident detection of token-burst-driven SLO violations, reduces noisy alerts by enabling burst-aware alerting windows, and gives customers a lower-latency signal path for critical observability. Release notes: introduce Observability Gateway to speed critical telemetry and token-slew meter for burst detection and alert optimization.
